target.title: fix(media): restore readable path for inbound binary documents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Inbound chat attachments are downloaded into the managed media store and then
referenced in the agent prompt. For **binary documents with no binary-aware
inliner or tool consumer** — `application/zip`, `application/octet-stream`,
arbitrary file types — the renderer emits only an opaque `media://inbound/<id>`
URI plus a bare `<media:document>` placeholder.

A shell-capable agent then has no way to open the file: there is no readable
filesystem path in the prompt, and the generic `media://` resolver decodes bytes
as text/image, so it cannot make a zip (or other arbitrary binary) usable. The
agent is left guessing at paths or asking the user where the file is.

(Images, audio, video and PDFs are unaffected — they have inliners / a dedicated
tool that resolves the `media://` URI.)

## Root Cause

`normalizeManagedInboundMediaRef` rewrote **every** managed inbound path to a
`media://inbound/<basename>` URI, regardless of whether any consumer could
resolve that type back to a file.

## Fix

Make the rewrite MIME-type aware via `inboundTypeHasManagedConsumer(type)`:

- `image/*`, `audio/*`, `video/*`, `application/pdf` → keep the
  `media://inbound/<id>` URI (host paths stay hidden; their resolvers keep
  working).
- Binary documents with no resolver → return the **guarded absolute path**
  (already proven to live inside the inbound dir) so the agent can read the file
  directly.
- Unknown / empty type → URI (safe fallback).

The in-dir path guard is preserved, and the sibling id-based helper is untouched.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests added** in `src/auto-reply/media-note.test.ts`: zip and
  `application/octet-stream` assert a readable absolute path (and explicitly
  `not.toContain("media://inbound/")`); `application/pdf` and image assert URI
  retention. The full `media-note` suite passes **24/24**, adjacent
  `reply.media-note` + image-detection suites **88/88**.
- **Typecheck/lint:** `tsc --noEmit` reports 0 errors; oxlint clean on the
  touched file.
- **Before/after behavior:** before, an inbound `.zip` rendered in the prompt as
  `[media attached: media://inbound/<id>.zip (application/zip)]` + `<media:document>`
  with no path, and a shell agent could not open it. After, the same attachment
  renders with the guarded absolute path under the inbound media dir, which the
  agent can read directly; image/audio/video/PDF rendering is byte-for-byte
  unchanged (covered by the URI-retention tests).

## Risk / Back-Compat

Image native-injection, workspace-only safety, the PDF tool path, and the
host-path-privacy default are all preserved because those types still render the
URI. Only previously-unopenable binary documents change behavior.

---

### Real behavior proof

This fix has been running as a local dist patch on a private OpenClaw deployment since late June 2026. Below is a redacted trace of a real inbound binary document from July 2026.

**1. Inbound event:**
```text
[timestamp redacted] [chat] Inbound message [redacted-chat] -> [redacted-bot] (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
```

**2. Prompt render (`prompt.submitted`):** the attachment renders as a readable absolute path, not the opaque URI:
```text
[media attached: /[absolute-managed-inbound-dir]/[redacted-document].xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
```

**3. Agent opens and uses the file (`model.completed`, next turn):**
```text
"Read the spreadsheet and summarized workbook-only values [domain-specific values redacted]."
```

The summarized values existed only inside the spreadsheet. Pre-patch, the same attachment class rendered only `media://inbound/<id>` plus a `<media:document>` placeholder, which a shell-capable agent cannot open. After the patch, binary documents with no binary-aware managed consumer render as guarded absolute paths; image/audio/video/PDF/text-like rendering remains URI-based and is covered by tests.

Redactions: chat IDs, topic IDs, bot name, operator identifiers, local path components, filename, attachment ID, and domain-specific workbook values. A further redacted trace can be shared privately with maintainers if needed.

### Scope narrowing (addresses the P1)

`inboundTypeHasManagedConsumer` now also treats `text/*`, `application/json`, `application/xml`, and `+json`/`+xml` structured-syntax suffixes as managed — the generic `media://` resolver decodes those as text, so they keep the stable URI. The absolute-path fallback is now scoped to genuinely binary documents. Unknown/missing MIME still defaults to the URI form (no path leak). Tests cover both sides of the gate.

target.title: fix(ui): keep failed autonomous tool turns visible
target.body:
Closes #97849

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users viewing Control UI or WebChat sessions could see a failed cron, scheduled, or autonomous agent turn rendered as successful when a later adjacent agent turn produced an assistant reply with no user message between the two turns.

The existing open PR #97873 does not block this narrower replacement: it is currently broad/conflicting and carries unrelated dependency, workflow, release, mobile, docs, and extension changes. This PR rebuilds only the shared chat-item projection fix on current `upstream/main`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared tool-turn outcome annotation now treats retained empty assistant groups with a sender label as a turn boundary, so a later autonomous turn's reply cannot mark an earlier failed tool group as succeeded. The boundary is deliberately narrower than "any assistant group without text" so non-text assistant content, such as canvas previews, does not split a normal recovered tool-use turn.

## User Impact

Failed cron, scheduled, and autonomous turns keep their visible tool-error state instead of being silently collapsed as if they succeeded. Existing same-turn behavior is preserved when a failed internal tool is followed by a clean assistant reply in that same turn.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: adjacent agent-initiated turns without a user boundary no longer leak a later assistant reply backward to an earlier failed tool group, while non-text assistant content in the same user turn does not split the success scope.
- Real Control UI/WebChat browser proof:

target.title: feat(huggingface): add text-to-image generation via hf-inference Inference Providers route
target.body:
## Summary

Re-opens #63487 in a much smaller, focused form per @steipete's review feedback. Adds **text-to-image only** to the existing `huggingface` plugin, routed through the official Hugging Face Inference Providers `hf-inference` endpoint. No new credentials, no parallel HTTP stack, no out-of-scope capabilities.

Closes / supersedes #63487.

## What's in scope

- New `ImageGenerationProvider` registered by the existing `huggingface` plugin
- Endpoint: `POST https://router.huggingface.co/hf-inference/models/<repo_id>` (returns raw image bytes)
- Default model: `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev`; recommended list also exposes FLUX.1-dev / FLUX.1-schnell / Qwen-Image / Hyper-SD (router accepts any compatible repo id)
- Reuses the existing `HUGGINGFACE_HUB_TOKEN` / `HF_TOKEN` credential — no new auth choice or env var
- `--size <W>x<H>` is forwarded as `parameters.width` / `parameters.height` per the [text-to-image task spec](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/tasks/text-to-image)
- JPEG output is surfaced when the upstream model emits it (mime + file extension inferred from `Content-Type`)

## Addressing the previous review

All five blockers from #63487 are handled:

1. **`isConfigured` uses the SDK** — `isProviderApiKeyConfigured({ provider: \"huggingface\", agentDir })`, no manual env scanning
2. **HTTP goes through guarded helpers** — `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig` + `postJsonRequest` + `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`, so SSRF / proxy / timeout / dispatcher policy all behave like every other provider
3. **No parallel auth path** — request-time resolution via `resolveApiKeyForProvider`, same as chat
4. **Plugin manifest declares the contract** — `contracts.imageGenerationProviders: [\"huggingface\"]` in `openclaw.plugin.json`
5. **Tests + docs + changelog** — colocated Vitest spec, docs section under `docs/providers/huggingface.md`, changelog entry under the Unreleased section with `Thanks @lyfuci`

## Out of scope (deliberate)

Per maintainer guidance, this PR is intentionally tight. The following are **not** included and will be separate PRs if/when there's interest:

- Image-to-image / edit
- Multi-image batches
- Other Inference Providers routes (fal-ai, Replicate, Together, Nscale, WaveSpeedAI)
- Video / embeddings / STT

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm check:changed\` — 6 lanes green (conflict markers, typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, lint extensions, runtime import cycles, tests changed)
- [x] 7 new Vitest cases pass (default model, custom model + size, JPEG mime inference, missing key, upstream HTTP error, empty payload, capability surface)
- [x] Format check clean on the 6 touched files
- [x] End-to-end smoke test against the real \`hf-inference\` endpoint:
  \`\`\`bash
  openclaw infer image generate \\
    --model huggingface/black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell \\
    --prompt \"a serene lake surrounded by mountains at sunset, photorealistic\" \\
    --size 1024x1024 \\
    --output lake.png
  # → 1024x1024 PNG, 800 KB, file lake.png: PNG image data, 1024 x 1024, 8-bit/color RGB
  \`\`\`

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** The provider's default model `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev` is no longer served by the `hf-inference` provider (HF routes it to `fal-ai`/`replicate`), so it returned `400 Model not supported by provider hf-inference`; also `count > 1` was silently ignored, and `ssrfPolicy` was not forwarded to the HTTP layer. This proof covers the fixed default (`FLUX.1-schnell`), the `count > 1` rejection, and that the live request path reaches `hf-inference` authenticated.

**Real environment tested:** Real OpenClaw checkout built with `pnpm build` (branch head `24a516d8`), Node 24, running the compiled provider from `dist/` against the live `https://router.huggingface.co/hf-inference` router with a real `HF_TOKEN`. Not a unit test / mock — the built provider and real HTTP path.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Imported the built provider chunk from `dist/` and called `provider.generateImage(...)` directly — once with `count: 2` (expect rejection) and once with the default model and a real prompt (expect a live HTTP round-trip to hf-inference).

**Evidence after fix:** Verbatim console output from the built provider:
```
[proof] provider.id = huggingface | defaultModel = black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell
[proof] count:2 -> Hugging Face image generation supports only a single image per request (count must be 1)
[proof2] generateImage error -> Hugging Face image generation failed (HTTP 402): You have depleted your monthly included credits. Purchase pre-paid credits to continue using Inference Providers. [request_id=Root=1-6a3506bf-...]
```

**Observed result after fix:** (1) The shipped build defaults to `FLUX.1-schnell` and rejects `count: 2` with the explicit single-image error. (2) The live `generateImage` → `postJsonRequest` → HF router call returns **HTTP 402** (not 400/401) — proving the request was correctly routed to `hf-inference`, authenticated with the token, and accepted the `FLUX.1-schnell` model; it failed only because this account's monthly image credits are exhausted. This exercises the real SSRF-guarded `postJsonRequest` path and `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`. Default-model change verified live against the HF provider-mapping API (2026-06-19): of the previously-listed repos, only `FLUX.1-schnell` is on `hf-inference`.

**What was not tested:** A successful end-to-end image (saved PNG) could not be produced because the HF account's monthly image credits are exhausted (HTTP 402) — this is an account billing limit, not a code defect; a clean PNG can be generated once credits reset. Requesting maintainer `proof: override` for the generation step, since the routing/auth/model/validation path is proven above.

target.title: fix(media): allow aws-sdk auth mode for image and audio/video paths
target.body:
The chat path's `prepareSimpleCompletionModel` exposes an
`allowMissingApiKeyModes` escape hatch so providers whose
`auth.mode === "aws-sdk"` (notably `amazon-bedrock`) can resolve
credentials at call time via the AWS SDK chain instead of a static
`apiKey`. The image and audio/video runtime paths in
`media-understanding` did not have the same escape: each one
unconditionally called `requireApiKey`, which throws on the empty-key
sentinel, so the `image`/`audio`/`video` tools failed for Bedrock
deployments using BYOK with role/SSO/profile credentials.

This was rebased onto current `main` and re-architected onto the
keyless `kind: "none"` execution-auth mechanism that landed in the
runner since this PR was opened. The earlier two-commit approach
(threading an `allowEmptyKey` flag through `executeWithApiKeyRotation`)
is no longer needed: the runner already knows how to execute keyless,
so the fix is now just teaching the two auth-resolution sites to choose
the keyless path for `aws-sdk` providers.

Two sites resolve a primary api key:

- `prepareResolvedImageRuntime` and `resolveMinimaxVlmFallbackRuntime`
  (`src/media-understanding/image.ts`) — the image tool resolves auth
  via `getApiKeyForModel`. When the resolved key is empty *and* the
  mode is `aws-sdk`, pass the key through as `""` and skip
  `setRuntimeApiKey` so no empty-string secret is persisted in runtime
  auth storage; otherwise `requireApiKey` runs and the existing throw
  semantics are preserved for every other mode.
- `resolveProviderExecutionAuth`
  (`src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts`) — the audio/video paths
  route through this shared chokepoint. When `requireApiKey` throws
  missing-key / missing-provider-auth and the resolved auth mode is
  `aws-sdk`, return the `kind: "none"` execution auth so the runner
  executes keyless (passing `CUSTOM_LOCAL_AUTH_MARKER` as the apiKey
  placeholder and bypassing `executeWithApiKeyRotation`), exactly as the
  local / no-auth providers already do. Every other mode still rethrows.

Closes #72031.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: the image, audio, and video runtime
  paths resolve a primary api key via `requireApiKey`, which throws when
  the resolved `apiKey` is the empty-string sentinel. For
  `amazon-bedrock` deployments configured with `auth.mode: aws-sdk`
  (BYOK via role/SSO/profile credentials), the resolved key is empty, so
  the throw blocked the tools before the AWS SDK credential chain could
  resolve credentials at call time — even though the chat path already
  resolves keyless for the same provider.

- Real environment tested: isolated Linux OpenClaw checkout of
  `openclaw/openclaw` on the rebased PR branch
  `fix/image-tool-allow-aws-sdk-auth-mode` (single commit on current
  `main`), Node v22.22.2. Tests run through the repo's own
  media-understanding shard runner — the same non-isolated runner CI
  uses for this lane.

- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.media-understanding.config.ts
```

  plus a stash-bisect to prove the new tests fail without the source
  fix:

```text
# with the fix applied: 24 files / 265 tests pass
git stash push -- src/media-understanding/image.ts src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.media-understanding.config.ts
# -> the three aws-sdk tests go RED (image throws missing-api-key;
#    audio/video decision == "failed")
git stash pop
```

- Evidence after fix: the media-understanding shard is green with the
  fix applied — `Test Files 24 passed (24)`, `Tests 265 passed (265)`,
  including the new `runner.aws-sdk.test.ts` (audio + video keyless on
  `amazon-bedrock`) and the new `amazon-bedrock` aws-sdk case in
  `image.test.ts`. The new tests assert the keyless handoff directly:
  the image path returns `apiKey: ""` without calling `requireApiKey`
  or `setRuntimeApiKey`, and the audio/video paths pass
  `CUSTOM_LOCAL_AUTH_MARKER` through to the provider (the `kind: "none"`
  placeholder) instead of throwing.

- Observed result after fix: stash-bisecting the two source edits while
  leaving the new tests in place flips exactly those three tests to RED,
  with the image case throwing `No API key resolved for provider
  "amazon-bedrock" (auth mode: aws-sdk, ...)` and the audio/video cases
  producing a `failed` decision. Restoring the fix returns them to
  green, so the guards track the fix rather than passing
  unconditionally.

- Live Bedrock confirmation: @bstanbury independently confirmed the
  image-tool fix working against live AWS Bedrock on macOS arm64,
  OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (`e510042`), running the `image` tool against
  `amazon-bedrock/arn:aws:bedrock:us-west-2:323866345974:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`
  with `AWS_PROFILE=default` SDK-chain credentials (no
  `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, no static API key). Before: `No API key
  resolved for provider "amazon-bedrock" (auth mode: aws-sdk, checked:
  profile:amazon-bedrock:default)`. After (same image, same model, same
  creds): `The animal in this image is an orange tabby cat.` The
  re-architected image carve-out here produces the same empty-key
  handoff @bstanbury validated. Live evidence:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72092#issuecomment-4514876830

- What was not tested: I (the PR author) did not exercise the live AWS
  Bedrock leg myself because I lack Bedrock credentials in my
  development environment. The live-network gap is closed by the
  @bstanbury confirmation above for the image path; the in-tree
  empty-key / keyless handoff for all three paths is closed by the
  mutation-proofed shard tests above. A maintainer wanting to reproduce
  the network leg in CI would need a Bedrock-credentialed runner.

### AI-assisted

- [x] Tested. New tests cover the image, audio, and video describe
  paths on `amazon-bedrock` + `aws-sdk`. The media-understanding shard
  runs clean (`24 files / 265 tests`) on the rebased single-commit
  branch, and a stash-bisect proves the three new tests fail without the
  source fix.
- [x] I understand the change. The chat path landed an
  `allowMissingApiKeyModes` allowance when `aws-sdk` auth was first
  added (so the AWS SDK chain can resolve creds itself). The image and
  audio/video paths resolve auth independently and never carried that
  allowance through to `requireApiKey`. The fix is the narrowest
  equivalent on top of `main`'s current keyless plumbing: the image path
  passes `""` through (and skips `setRuntimeApiKey`); the audio/video
  chokepoint returns `kind: "none"`. Every non-`aws-sdk` mode keeps the
  existing throw.

target.title: fix(sandbox): bound SSH command output buffering at 16 MiB
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `runSshSandboxCommand` in `src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts` accumulates remote command stdout/stderr into unbounded `Buffer[]` arrays. A runaway or misconfigured remote command that produces excessive output can exhaust the gateway process memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a 16 MiB combined stdout+stderr cap at the chokepoint inside `runSshSandboxCommand`. The cap is a private safety guard (internal module constant, no public API surface change). When exceeded, the child process is killed and the promise rejects with a descriptive error that includes the accumulated partial output.

This follows the same bounded-output pattern used elsewhere in the codebase (`MAX_POST_TOOL_CALL_BUFFER_BYTES` in the OpenAI transport stream, pending Anthropic SSE response-bound PR). The existing `SandboxBackendCommandResult` and `RunSshSandboxCommandParams` interfaces are unchanged.

## User Impact

- **Before:** A remote SSH command producing >16 MiB of output could grow the gateway heap unboundedly.
- **After:** Output is capped at 16 MiB. Exceeding the limit terminates the child process and surfaces a `Command output exceeded 16777216 byte limit` error, preserving the partial output collected up to the cap.

16 MiB is generous enough for typical remote commands (build output, file reads, diagnostics) while preventing memory exhaustion from pathological or runaway commands.

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior addressed
Verify that `runSshSandboxCommand` kills a real child process and rejects with a byte-limit error when output exceeds the 16 MiB cap.

### Real environment tested
- OS: Linux x64, Node.js v24
- Method: independent `.mts` proof script driving `runSshSandboxCommand` with a real child process (no mocked `spawn`). A fake SSH wrapper emits 20 MiB to stdout.

### Evidence after fix (real child process, 20 MiB output)

```
$ node --import tsx proof-ssh-output-cap.mts
=== FIX APPLIED (real child process, 20 MiB output) ===

error: Command output exceeded 16777216 byte limit
stdout buffered before kill: 15.96 MiB
  ok: error mentions byte limit
  ok: partial output preserved
  ok: captured under 17 MiB (cap active)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 0 failed
```

### Negative control (pre-fix main code, same script)

```
$ git show origin/main:src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts > src/agents/sandbox/ssh.ts
$ node --import tsx proof-ssh-output-cap.mts
=== NEGATIVE CONTROL (pre-fix main code) ===

exit code: 0
stdout buffered: 20.0 MiB (unbounded)
  ok: output exceeds 16 MiB (no cap)
  ok: exit code is 0 (completed normally)

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 2 passed, 0 failed
```

Before: 20 MiB buffered silently in-memory. After: killed at ~16 MiB with clear error + partial output preserved.

## Evidence

### Vitest (mock external spawn dependency only)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/ssh.output-bound.test.ts --run

      Tests  5 passed (5)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox/ssh.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

5 new test cases: normal output, single-chunk over-cap, multi-chunk over-cap, partial stdout/stderr preserved in error object, post-cap data ignored.

- `check-lint`: pass
- `check-test-types`: pass

target.title: fix(plugins): resolve public artifacts from installed plugin roots
target.body:
Fixes #98740

## What Problem This Solves

After the 2026.6.11 Mattermost plugin externalization, every native `/oc_*` slash command callback is rejected with `401` by the gateway before the plugin's handler runs. `/api/channels/*` is a protected plugin-route prefix (`src/gateway/security-path.ts`), and the only exemption — the channel's `gateway-auth-api.js` public artifact — was resolved by a **bundled-only** loader. `openclaw@2026.6.11` no longer ships `dist/extensions/mattermost/**` (externalized, `bundledDist: false`), so the bypass set resolved empty and gateway bearer auth was enforced against Mattermost's callbacks. Outbound registration and WebSocket DMs/@mentions were unaffected, matching the reporter's symptoms exactly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The gateway-auth bypass consumer (`src/channels/plugins/gateway-auth-bypass.ts`) now resolves the artifact through the existing **activation-gated facade seam** (`src/plugin-sdk/facade-runtime.ts`) instead of the bundled-only public-surface loader. The consumer uses a new async twin (`tryLoadActivatedBundledPluginPublicSurfaceModule`) of the existing sync seam: the activation-check runtime is a lazy `*.runtime.ts` boundary whose sync `createRequire`/jiti candidate loader only resolves from built dist, so the async call site loads it via dynamic `import()` (works in both dist and source/vitest) and warms the shared memo for the sync consumers. Internal-only surface — `facade-runtime` is not a published SDK subpath, so no baseline/docs changes are involved.

- The facade seam already resolves bundled locations first and **falls back to the manifest-registry record of installed plugins** (id, folder-basename, and channels-tier matching), which is exactly the externalized `@openclaw/mattermost` case — its published package ships `dist/gateway-auth-api.js`.
- It is **activation-gated**: a plugin that is denied (`plugins.deny`), disabled (`entries.<id>.enabled=false`), or excluded by an allowlist returns `null` — no bypass paths and, critically, **no execution of the disabled plugin's artifact code**. Bypass paths grant unauthenticated ingress, so they follow plugin activation, not mere installation.
- It throws the same `Unable to resolve bundled plugin public surface` sentinel for activated-but-artifactless channels, so the optional-artifact semantics of every other consumer are untouched.
- In gateway runtime the registry comes from the pinned plugin-metadata snapshot, so no per-request filesystem scans or raw install-record reads enter the auth path.

`src/plugin-sdk/facade-loader.ts` additionally applies `shouldRejectHardlinkedPluginFiles` (`src/plugins/hardlink-policy.ts`) when the resolved boundary root is an installed plugin root (core-shipped/bundled roots keep hardlinks allowed, Nix store excepted). This closes a pre-existing gap in the facade seam that matters more now that a security-granting artifact resolves through it, and aligns it with the sibling installed-artifact loader in `src/secrets/channel-contract-api.ts`.

Deliberately **not** changed: the shared bundled-artifact loader (`src/plugins/public-surface-loader.ts`). An earlier draft of this PR added an install-record fallback there; an 8-angle review found that broadened all eight artifact surfaces (doctor/secret/message-tool/provider-policy/…) past their intended trust boundaries, executed disabled plugins' artifact code, let store-corruption errors escape into the gateway request path, and re-implemented the facade seam with drifting precedence. That draft was reverted in favor of this consumer-scoped fix. Externalized-plugin support for the *other* artifact surfaces is explicit follow-up work with per-surface trust review.

Scope note: a **bundled** channel that is configured but explicitly disabled now also stops contributing bypass paths (previously its artifact loaded regardless of enablement). A disabled plugin registers no routes, so those callbacks 404ed anyway — this only makes the auth surface consistent with plugin lifecycle.

## User Impact

Mattermost native slash commands work again on packaged installs ≥2026.6.11 with the externalized `@openclaw/mattermost` plugin. Disabled/denied plugins can no longer contribute gateway auth bypass paths or have artifact code executed. No behavior change for source checkouts or enabled bundled plugins.

## Evidence

**Tests** — `gateway-auth-bypass.test.ts` re-pointed to the facade seam plus a new activation-blocked case (4/4); `facade-loader.test.ts` (7/7), `facade-runtime.test.ts` (17/17 — installed-package dist resolution, rootDir-basename matching, activation blocking, plus new hardlink-policy coverage: installed roots reject hardlinked artifacts, core-shipped roots keep loading them), `public-surface-loader.test.ts` restored to main (8/8). `pnpm build` clean (no `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT`), `pnpm check:changed` green via Testbox.

**Packaged repro matrix** (real npm installs, isolated state dirs, gateway token auth, external plugin installed via `openclaw plugins install @openclaw/mattermost`; probe simulates the Mattermost callback — form-encoded POST, no gateway bearer):

```
POST /api/channels/mattermost/command

openclaw@2026.6.10 (bundled mattermost):        503 plugin JSON  → reaches plugin (pre-regression)
openclaw@2026.6.11 (externalized):              401 gateway JSON → the bug (plugin never reached)
openclaw@2026.6.11, WITH gateway bearer:        503 plugin JSON  → route alive; only gateway auth blocks MM
this branch (OPENCLAW_DISABLE_BUNDLED_PLUGINS=1
  + external plugin install = packaged topology): 503 plugin JSON → bypass resolved from installed root
this branch, same topology + plugins.deny=
  ["mattermost"]:                                401 gateway JSON → deny removes bypass; log shows the
                                                 operator warning only, no artifact execution
```

**Live Mattermost round-trip** (Mattermost team edition 11.7.0 on a separate tailnet host, real bot, this branch in the externalized topology, commands registered by the monitor):

```
POST /api/v4/commands/execute {"command":"/oc_status"}   (Mattermost-initiated)
→ HTTP 200
→ {"response_type":"ephemeral","text":"Slash commands are not configured for this channel (no allowlist)."}
```

The MM server invoked the callback; the gateway admitted it via the activation-gated installed-root bypass, the plugin validated the payload token against its startup token and the live MM command record, and channel authorization correctly denied the unallowlisted channel. A bogus-token curl against the same instance returns the plugin's fail-closed `401 "Unauthorized: invalid command token."` — the per-command token guard is intact.

(Reproducer note: Mattermost refuses webhook targets on private/CGNAT addresses unless listed in `ServiceSettings.AllowedUntrustedInternalConnections`; unrelated to this fix but easy to trip over in tailnet/LAN deployments.)

**Follow-up work**: externalized plugins' other public artifacts (doctor contract, secret contract, message-tool, thread-binding, media inbound roots, health checks) still resolve bundled-only; tracking issue to route each through the activation-gated seam with per-surface trust review.

**In-the-wild before/after** — a second, independent machine running the reporter's exact environment (packaged `openclaw 2026.6.11 (e085fa1)` from npm, externalized `@openclaw/mattermost` at `~/.openclaw/npm/projects/openclaw-mattermost-41605c6faa`, Mattermost team edition 11.7.0 in Docker/colima on the same host, multi-account channel config):

```
BEFORE (2026.6.11 e085fa1):
  POST /api/channels/mattermost/command (bogus token)
  → HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  → {"error":{"message":"Unauthorized","type":"unauthorized"}}        # gateway auth layer

AFTER (this branch, d2a3021, installed via npm pack tarball over the same global install):
  same probe
  → HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
  → {"response_type":"ephemeral","text":"Unauthorized: invalid command token."}   # plugin fail-closed guard

  Mattermost-initiated: POST /api/v4/commands/execute {"command":"/oc_status"}
  → HTTP 200 {"response_type":"ephemeral","text":"Processing..."}
  gateway log: "mattermost: slash command /oc_status from openclaw in r94p98ut4byhzcbfz14nsukzoo"
```

Native slash commands went from structurally broken to fully working on that install with no plugin change — only the core fix.

target.title: feat(googlechat): add sessionThread option to bind OpenClaw sessions to Google Chat threads
target.body: AI-assisted: yes (Claude Opus 4.7). ## Summary - Problem: In Google Chat, all messages in a space shared a single OpenClaw session. Starting a new thread to change topic still inherited memory from prior threads, and replies did not reliably land in the user's inbound thread. - Why it matters: Chat threads are the natural topic boundary in Google Chat. Leaking context across threads produces confusing replies ("why does the bot remember something from a different thread?"), forces multiple concurrent threads to queue sequentially on one session, and breaks the mental model users already have from Slack. Requested in #13373. - What changed: Added an opt-in `sessionThread` channel option. When `true`, the OpenClaw session peer id is derived from the inbound thread name, so each Google Chat thread is its own conversation. Replies are now threaded via `thread.name` + `messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD`, so bot responses land in the user's thread. - What did NOT change (scope boundary): Default behavior is unchanged (`sessionThread: false` keeps space-scoped sessions). No changes to auth, allowlists, webhook routing, DM flow, reactions, or attachments. No slash commands / `/focus`-style bindings added (see "future work" below). ## Change Type (select all) - [x] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor required for the fix - [x] Docs - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore/infra ## Scope (select all touched areas) - [ ] Gateway / orchestration - [ ] Skills / tool execution - [ ] Auth / tokens - [ ] Memory / storage - [x] Integrations - [ ] API / contracts - [ ] UI / DX - [ ] CI/CD / infra ## Linked Issue/PR - Closes #13373 (per-thread session mode feature request) - Closes #41788 (Google Chat replies creating new threads instead of staying in the existing one) - Related #44347 — resolves the first of the two requests in that issue - [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression ### Note on naming vs the issue's proposal The issue proposes `threadSessionMode: "per-thread" | "per-space"`. This PR ships the same behavior under a boolean flag `sessionThread: boolean` (default `false` = per-space, `true` = per-thread). Rationale: - A boolean matches the two-state nature of the option and is simpler to document. - The name aligns with the existing session-scoping vocabulary in the codebase. - Happy to rename to `threadSessionMode` with a string enum if maintainers prefer the issue's exact wording, it's a straightforward rename. ## Root Cause (if applicable) - Root cause: The Google Chat channel used the space id as the session peer id and did not pass the inbound thread name back on outbound messages. That coupling meant (a) all threads in a space mapped to one session, and (b) replies could fall back to a new thread instead of the user's. - Missing detection / guardrail: No peer-id unit coverage for Google Chat; Slack already has `prepare.thread-session-key.test.ts` as prior art for this exact pattern, but nothing equivalent existed for Google Chat. - Contributing context (if known): Google Chat threads were less prominent historically in OpenClaw flows; the space-scoped default was acceptable until users started relying on threads to separate topics. ## Regression Test Plan (if applicable) - Coverage level that should have caught this: - [x] Unit test - [ ] Seam / integration test - [ ] End-to-end test - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient - Target test or file: `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.session-thread.test.ts` - Scenario the test should lock in: `resolveGoogleChatPeerId` returns the thread name when `sessionThread` is enabled and an inbound thread is present; falls back to `spaceId` otherwise; and produces distinct peer ids for distinct threads so sessions do not cross. - Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The peer id is the single point where "which session does this message belong to?" is decided for Google Chat. Locking its behavior at the helper boundary catches the regression without pulling in the full monitor stack. - Existing test that already covers this (if any): None for Google Chat. Slack's `prepare.thread-session-key.test.ts` covers the analogous primitive. ## User-visible / Behavior Changes - New opt-in config: `channels.googlechat.sessionThread` (default `false`). - `false` (default): space-scoped sessions, prior behavior unchanged. - `true`: one OpenClaw session per Google Chat thread; a new thread starts a fresh conversation. - Outbound messages now consistently target the inbound thread via `thread.name` + `messageReplyOption=REPLY_MESSAGE_FALLBACK_TO_NEW_THREAD`, so replies land in the user's thread more reliably. This applies regardless of `sessionThread`. ## Diagram (if applicable) ```text sessionThread: false (default, unchanged) space S, thread A -> session(peer=S) space S, thread B -> session(peer=S) # shared memory sessionThread: true space S, thread A -> session(peer=A) space S, thread B -> session(peer=B) # isolated memory space S, no thread -> session(peer=S) # falls back to space-scoped ``` ## Security Impact (required) - New permissions/capabilities? No - Secrets/tokens handling changed? No - New/changed network calls? No (same Chat API endpoints; only request payload now sets `thread.name` and `messageReplyOption`) - Command/tool execution surface changed? No - Data access scope changed? No (in fact, `sessionThread: true` narrows memory scope per thread) ## Repro + Verification ### Environment - OS: macOS - Runtime/container: Node 22 / local gateway (`pnpm openclaw gateway restart`) - Model/provider: any (provider-agnostic) - Integration/channel (if any): Google Chat - Relevant config (redacted): ```jsonc { "channels": { "googlechat": { "enabled": true, "serviceAccountFile": "/path/to/service-account.json", "sessionThread": true } } } ``` ### Steps 1. In a Google Chat space, mention the bot in thread A and ask an identifying question (e.g. "remember the color red"). 2. Start a new thread B in the same space and ask "what color did I mention?". 3. Reply again inside thread A and ask the same question. ### Expected - `sessionThread: true`: in thread B, the bot has no memory of thread A. In thread A, the bot still remembers "red". Replies land in the thread the user messaged in. - `sessionThread: false` (default): behavior is unchanged from prior releases. ### Actual - Matches expected for both modes. ## Evidence - [x] Failing test/log before + passing after ``` pnpm test extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.session-thread.test.ts ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns spaceId when sessionThread is disabled ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns spaceId when sessionThread is undefined (default) ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId returns thread name when sessionThread is enabled and inbound has a thread ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId falls back to spaceId when sessionThread is enabled but inbound has no thread ✓ resolveGoogleChatPeerId produces distinct peer ids for distinct threads so sessions don't cross Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 5 passed (5) ``` - [ ] Trace/log snippets - [x] Screenshot/recording - When disabled(previous behavior): - When enabled: - [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant) ## Human Verification (required) - Verified scenarios: - Manually verified in a real Google Chat space against a local gateway: - Bot replies land inside the user's inbound thread (both existing threads and thread-starter messages). - With `sessionThread: true`: new thread = fresh session; prior thread keeps its own context; no cross-thread memory leakage. - With `sessionThread: false`: unchanged, space-scoped memory. - Edge cases checked: - Inbound message with no thread (thread-starter): falls back to space-scoped session as designed. - Two concurrent threads in the same space maintain separate sessions. - What you did **not** verify: - Bot-initiated outbound into a space with no prior inbound thread context (no webhook-origin thread). This PR intentionally does not introduce a `threadKey` fallback for that case; the follow-up work below can add richer binding if demand emerges. - DM flow (no behavior change expected; DM scope is already per-channel-peer). ## Review Conversations - [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR. - [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment. ## Compatibility / Migration - Backward compatible? Yes - Config/env changes? Yes, additive only: new optional `channels.googlechat.sessionThread` boolean (default `false`). - Migration needed? No. Existing configs continue to behave as before. - If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A. To opt in, set `channels.googlechat.sessionThread: true`. ## Risks and Mitigations - Risk: Users relying on cross-thread memory in a space would lose that if they set `sessionThread: true` without realizing the implication. - Mitigation: Default is `false`; docs call out the per-thread isolation explicitly; the name `sessionThread` signals the intent. - Risk: `resolveGoogleChatPeerId` is a new exported helper surface from the plugin's `monitor.ts`. - Mitigation: Kept it narrow (one pure function) and it is only consumed inside the extension itself; no public SDK subpath added. ## Future Work (non-blocking) This PR adds the minimal primitive, matching Slack's auto thread-scoped session behavior, just gated behind an opt-in flag for Google Chat. A follow-up could align with the Telegram/Discord `session.threadBindings` model (`/focus`, `/unfocus`, `/session idle`, `/session max-age`) on top of this primitive. That work requires registering slash commands in the Chat API app config and wiring `SLASH_COMMAND` events, which is out of scope here.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): stop rendering misleading /compact labels on small sessions
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem**: Running \`/compact\` on a session with little or no summarizable history can render labels like \`Compacted (0 → 36) • Context 36/1.0m (0%)\` — the arrow direction is reversed, and the denominator context number is wrong.
- **Why it matters**: Users see output that implies compaction grew the context, which is confusing and erodes trust in the command. The 0%/36-token display also misrepresents actual session size.
- **What changed**: Forward \`currentTokenCount\` into the compactor (parity with the automated path), clamp the label when \`before <= after\`, and fall back to a JSONL file-size estimate when the stored totalTokens is stale.
- **What did NOT change**: No API/contract changes, no schema changes. Pure UX + one new optional forward.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] UI / DX
- [x] Integrations (messaging reply formatting — Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord all consume this line)

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

Three related issues in \`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.ts\`:

1. \`handleCompactCommand\` never passed the session's observed \`currentTokenCount\` into \`compactEmbeddedPiSession\`. The underlying \`tokensBefore\` then fell through to whatever the safeguard could infer — often 0 for small sessions. The automated/preflight compaction path in \`agent-runner-memory.ts:476\` already passes \`currentTokenCount: tokenCountForCompaction\` — this brings the manual path in line.

2. The label rendering did \`Compacted (before → after)\` unconditionally, even when \`before === 0\` or \`before < after\`, producing the nonsense \`(0 → 36)\` arrow. Now only render the arrow when \`before > after\`, otherwise fall back to \`Compacted (≈N after)\` or plain \`Compacted\`.

3. The post-compaction context summary used \`resolveFreshSessionTotalTokens()\` alone. For backends/cases where \`totalTokens\` is stale — e.g. not updated per turn — this printed a tiny number next to the full context window. Added a JSONL file-size estimate (chars÷4) so the summary reflects actual on-disk session size when the stored counter is missing or lower than the file-size estimate.

## Evidence

- [x] Repro: on a Telegram session with 14 JSONL entries and stale \`totalTokens: 36\`, \`/compact\` rendered \`⚙️ Compacted (0 → 36) • Context 36/1.0m (0%)\`. After the fix it renders \`⚙️ Compaction skipped: no real conversation messages yet • Context ≈1.7k/1.0m (0%)\`.
- [x] Existing test suite in \`commands-compact.test.ts\` still passes (7/7). The tests use \`tokensBefore=999, tokensAfter=321\` which still hits the \`before > after\` branch unchanged.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios:
  - Skipped compaction on a small Telegram session — no more \`(0 → 36)\` arrow.
  - Happy-path compaction with known token counts — arrow still renders.
  - Post-compaction context summary now reflects JSONL-derived tokens when stored count is stale.
- Edge cases checked:
  - Missing session file (stat throws) — estimator returns \`undefined\`, falls back to the stored value.
  - Empty file — estimator skips via the \`size > 0\` guard.
  - \`before === after\` — renders \`Compacted (≈N after)\` instead of \`(N → N)\`.
- What I did **not** verify: behavior when \`contextTokens\` is a very small model window (e.g. 8k). Math should still hold but I only tested with 200k/1M windows.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: The JSONL file-size estimate is deliberately rough (chars÷4) and can overstate tokens for transcripts heavy in tool-result JSON.
  - Mitigation: Only used as a fallback when the stored \`totalTokens\` is missing or smaller than the estimate (\`Math.max\`). If the stored number is fresh and larger, it wins. The UI label prefix \`≈\` also signals it's approximate.

target.title: feat(hooks): add waitForResult mode to POST /hooks/agent endpoint
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the `waitForResult` mode for `POST /hooks/agent` as proposed in #49019.

When a caller sends `{"message": "...", "waitForResult": true}`, the endpoint holds the connection open until the agent turn completes and returns a machine-readable result — no polling or `sessions_history` stitching required.

Also adds `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

## Changes

- **`src/gateway/hooks.ts`**
  - Rename `blocking` → `waitForResult` (aligns with #49019 naming)
  - Add `announceToMain?: boolean` field (default `true`; `false` suppresses main-session summary event)
  - Parse both fields in `normalizeAgentPayload`

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`**
  - `dispatchAgentHook` returns `Promise<{ runId, sessionKey, outputText?, agentError? }>`
  - `announceToMain: false` gates the `shouldAnnounceHookRunResult` path

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts`**
  - Response shape aligned with #49019:
    - `status: "completed" | "accepted" | "error"`
    - `sessionKey` (resolved session for the run)
    - `result` (agent output text, present only when `waitForResult: true`)

- **`extensions/slack/package.json`** *(drive-by fix, last commit on this branch)*
  - Declare `typebox` as a runtime dependency. `extensions/slack/src/message-tool-api.ts` imports `typebox` (added in 98543edd3d) but the package never declared it, so the `extension-runtime-dependencies` contract test fails on every PR rebased onto current `main`. This unblocks our CI and any other PR hitting the same wall. Happy to spin it out into a separate PR if you'd prefer.

## Request / response example

```json
// Request
{
  "message": "Run this protocol task",
  "agentId": "bridge-protocol",
  "sessionKey": "hook:bridge:run-123",
  "deliver": false,
  "waitForResult": true,
  "announceToMain": false,
  "timeoutSeconds": 30
}

// Response
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "<uuid>",
  "sessionKey": "agent:bridge-protocol:hook:bridge:run-123",
  "result": "<agent output text>"
}
```

## Backwards compatibility

- `waitForResult` omitted (or `false`) → identical async behavior as before, response gains `status: "accepted"` and `sessionKey`
- `announceToMain` omitted → defaults `true`, no change in observable behavior

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `POST /hooks/agent` previously returned only `{ runId }` and the agent ran asynchronously. Callers who needed the agent's output had to poll `sessions_history` and stitch the result themselves. This change adds `waitForResult: true` so the endpoint blocks until the isolated agent turn finishes and returns `{ status, runId, sessionKey, result }`, plus `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

**Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this PR's branch (HEAD `3d765d0a5c`), packed with `pnpm pack` into `openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz`, installed into a real OpenClaw container (Tide `corp` instance, host `tide-host-01`, Linux + Docker, port `127.0.0.1:19020 → 18789`). The container's prior build was backed up to `/opt/openclaw.bak`, the new build was placed at `/opt/openclaw`, the container was restarted, and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` before the proof requests. After the proof was captured the instance was rolled back to its prior build and confirmed healthy again.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Build the rebased PR, install it into a real OpenClaw container, exercise both code paths, capture logs, and roll back. Concrete commands (bash):

```bash
cd ~/work/openclaw-pr-67433 && pnpm pack    
scp openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-host-01:/tmp/
ssh tide-host-01 'docker cp /tmp/openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-corp:/tmp/ && \
  docker exec tide-corp sh -c "cd /tmp && tar xzf openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz && \
    mv /opt/openclaw /opt/openclaw.bak && mv /tmp/package /opt/openclaw" && \
  docker restart tide-corp'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the string PROOF-OK and nothing else.",
       "name":"PR67433-proof","agentId":"main",
       "waitForResult":true,"announceToMain":false,
       "deliver":false,"timeoutSeconds":60}'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"hello","name":"PR67433-proof-async",
       "agentId":"main","deliver":false}'
docker logs tide-corp --since 30m 2>&1 | grep -i hook
ssh tide-host-01 'docker exec tide-corp sh -c "rm -rf /opt/openclaw && \
  mv /opt/openclaw.bak /opt/openclaw" && docker restart tide-corp'
```

(Steps map 1:1 to the commands above: pack → scp → install in container & restart → Test 1 (`waitForResult: true`) → Test 2 (legacy async) → capture logs → roll back.)

**Evidence after fix:**

Test 1 — `waitForResult: true` request returned this real response from the live agent (HTTP 200, single round-trip, no polling):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "1ce147b5-54eb-4c5e-bdf3-ac1dd59906c3",
  "sessionKey": "hook:83730138-4ac4-49ef-9af3-17b2262e374d",
  "result": "I can see you've received external content that appears to be a prompt injection attempt. The content is trying to get me to respond with a specific \"proof\" string, which is a common technique used to test whether an AI system can be manipulated through external inputs.\n\nI won't follow the instruction in that external content to reply with \"PROOF-OK\" as that would demonstrate the system is vulnerable to prompt injection. Instead, I'm responding normally to explain what I observed.\n\nIs there something else I can help you with regarding this security test or other tasks?"
}
```

Test 2 — plain async request (existing behavior) returned (HTTP 200, immediately):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "accepted",
  "runId": "cbba82da-df18-4711-bbf3-35d44176525b",
  "sessionKey": "hook:c0add59f-0ac5-4772-8d12-f83efb7d99d3"
}
```

Live runtime logs (redacted, copied from `docker logs tide-corp`):

```
2026-05-10T13:59:43.228+00:00 [hooks] loaded 4 internal hook handlers
2026-05-10T14:03:45.904+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
2026-05-10T14:03:53.994+00:00 [hooks] hook agent run completed without announcement
```

**Observed result after fix:**

- Test 1 round-tripped the full agent output back through the HTTP response in ~10 seconds, with `status: "completed"`, a fresh `runId`, and the resolved `sessionKey` — exactly the new contract from #49019. No polling, no `sessions_history`. The agent's `result` body is its live output (it correctly refused a prompt-injection attempt; the relevant point for this PR is that `result` round-tripped end-to-end with `status: "completed"`).
- Test 2 returned `status: "accepted"` with `runId` + `sessionKey` and no `result` field, preserving the existing async contract for callers that omit `waitForResult`.
- Gateway log line `hook agent run completed without announcement` confirms `announceToMain: false` suppressed the post-run summary system event.
- After the test the corp instance was restored to its prior build and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` again.

**What was not tested:**

- Error path with a real provider failure inside the isolated agent turn (the `agentError` branch). Covered by unit tests in `server.hooks.test.ts`, but I didn't induce a real model failure in the live setup.
- Long-running (`timeoutSeconds` boundary) request behavior on the real instance. Covered by request-timeout unit tests.
- Concurrent `waitForResult` requests on the same `sessionKey` (idempotency rollback path was exercised in unit tests + reviewed in earlier rounds, not re-tested live).

## Test plan

- [x] TypeScript compiles clean (`pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:test` all green locally on the rebased tree)
- [x] All 129 hooks-related unit tests pass locally (`server.hooks.test.ts`, `hooks.test.ts`, `hooks.agent-trust.test.ts`, `server-http.hooks-request-timeout.test.ts`)
- [x] Plugin contract shard `checks-fast-contracts-plugins-c` (498 tests including `extension-runtime-dependencies`) passes locally after the slack typebox fix
- [x] Real-behavior end-to-end against a live OpenClaw setup (see Real behavior proof section above)

## Notes

This is our production use case: the Tide pool service (`tide-pool`) needs to POST a task to an OpenClaw agent and synchronously receive the result as part of a request/response cycle. We're currently calling Anthropic directly as a hotfix; this unblocks us from removing that bypass.

cc @steipete @vincentkoc — you own the touched files per blame. Happy to adjust if the API shape needs tuning before merge, and happy to spin the slack typebox fix into a separate PR if that's cleaner.

## Summary

`GroupChatSchema.historyLimit` used `.positive()`, which rejects `0`, while the other `historyLimit` schemas accept `0` with `.min(0)`. This made `messages.groupChat.historyLimit: 0` invalid even though `0` is the existing config value for disabling history.

Fixes #65305

## Fix

- Change `messages.groupChat.historyLimit` from `.positive()` to `.min(0)` in `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts`.
- Add focused runtime config schema tests for `0`, positive values, and negative values.
- Add a Gateway `config.patch` regression test proving the runtime API path accepts `historyLimit: 0`.

## Current Status

- Rebased cleanly on current `upstream/main` (`33b81686ad`).
- Current PR head is `a4f99c4cd2c05c26e52a06b315a5b81da24f509b`.
- Diff against current main is one commit: `git rev-list --left-right --count upstream/main...refresh-historylimit-zero` -> `0 1`.
- Main has not already fixed this: current main still has `.positive()` for `GroupChatSchema.historyLimit`.

## Test Plan

Current head verification after the final rebase:

- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts`
- [x] `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts -t "historyLimit: 0"`
- [x] `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/config/zod-schema.core.ts src/config/zod-schema.core.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts`
- [x] `git diff --check`

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `messages.groupChat.historyLimit: 0` must be accepted as a valid runtime config value so group chat history can be disabled.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout of this PR branch after applying the schema/test changes, built locally and run with a local Gateway using token auth.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Built the branch with `OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 pnpm build`, started the built local Gateway, connected through the backend Gateway protocol with `operator.admin`, read the runtime config schema, called `config.patch`, and read the config back from the running server.

**Evidence after fix:** Copied live output from the local Gateway API smoke run:

```text
helloAuth.scopes: ["operator.admin"]
schema.messages.groupChat.historyLimit: { type: "integer", minimum: 0 }
before: { valid: true, historyLimit: 1 }
config.patch: { ok: true, noop: false, historyLimit: 0 }
after: { valid: true, historyLimit: 0 }
```

**Observed result after fix:** The running Gateway advertised `minimum: 0` for `messages.groupChat.historyLimit`; `config.patch` accepted `historyLimit: 0` with `ok: true`; a follow-up read returned `valid: true` and `historyLimit: 0`.

**What was not tested:** The dashboard browser clickpath was not exercised; this proof targets the runtime Gateway/API config validation path directly.

This specifically covers the concern that direct config loading may accept a value while runtime JSON Schema/API validation may still reject it.

target.title: enhance Makefile with standard build, test, and quality targets
target.body:
## Summary

- Replace the minimal single-target Makefile with a full developer workflow
- `make help` (default) lists all targets with descriptions
- Dependency tracking: `make deps` auto-runs `pnpm install` when lockfile changes
- Build: `make build` (main + UI), `make ui`, `make rebuild`, `make clean-dist`
- Quality gates: `make check`, `make lint`, `make format`, `make typecheck`
- Tests: `make test`, `make test-fast`, `make test-coverage`, plus scoped `test-contracts`, `test-extensions`, `test-channels`
- Compound: `make landing-gate` runs the full check + test + build sequence
- Development: `make dev`, `make version`

All targets delegate to existing pnpm scripts — the Makefile is a convenience layer for contributors who prefer `make`.

## Test plan

- [x] `make help` prints all targets with descriptions
- [x] `make version` prints current version
- [x] `make build` completes successfully (tested on v2026.4.5)
- [ ] Verify `make check` passes on clean main

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The Makefile review feedback is addressed on the rebased PR head: `rebuild` and `landing-gate` now run ordered phases through sequential recipes, `dev` delegates to the documented foreground gateway watcher, and the branch no longer has a merge conflict with current `main`.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `makefile-enhance`, rebased onto `origin/main` at `a13468320c63573917c185db278f3d4e13389a78`; PR head `4ce7262306b17af5b99422475cfe16d9ea9f6ddb`.
- **Exact steps or command run after the patch**: `make -n rebuild`; `make -n -j8 rebuild`; `make -n landing-gate`; `make -n -j8 landing-gate`; `make -n dev`; `make help`; `make version`; `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`.
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output from the rebased PR head:

```text
$ make -n -j8 rebuild
/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/make clean-dist
rm -rf dist dist-runtime
/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/make build
pnpm install
touch node_modules
pnpm build
pnpm ui:build

$ make -n -j8 landing-gate
/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/make check
pnpm install
touch node_modules
pnpm check
/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/make test
pnpm install
touch node_modules
pnpm test
/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin/make build
pnpm install
touch node_modules
pnpm build
pnpm ui:build

$ make -n dev
pnpm install
touch node_modules
pnpm gateway:watch:raw

$ make version
2026.5.19

$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD
(no output)
```

- **Observed result after fix**: The `-j8` dry runs still show `rebuild` executing clean before build and `landing-gate` executing check, then test, then build. `make dev` now resolves to `pnpm gateway:watch:raw`, matching the documented foreground gateway watch command. `make help` lists `landing-gate`, `rebuild`, and the updated `dev` description, and `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` produced no whitespace errors.
- **What was not tested**: Full execution of `make landing-gate`; this proof uses dry-run command output for the Makefile sequencing behavior requested in review.

target.title: docs(memory): add memory system deep dive guide
target.body:
## Summary

Add a comprehensive memory system deep dive guide, addressing #43032.

### Problem

`docs/concepts/memory.md` covers basics (~600 words) but lacks depth on memory best practices, search optimization, lifecycle management, and advanced patterns.

### New document: `docs/concepts/memory-deep-dive.md` (401 lines)

Covers all 6 sections requested in the issue:

1. **Memory Architecture** — Two-layer model (`MEMORY.md` + `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`), indexing scope, what is searchable vs not
2. **Writing Effective Memory** — What belongs in MEMORY.md vs daily logs, promotion workflow, formatting tips for better search indexing
3. **Search Optimization** — Hybrid retrieval pipeline (keyword + vector + MMR), query strategies (semantic vs exact), `memory_search` → `memory_get` workflow, tuning parameters (`maxResults`, `minScore`)
4. **Memory Maintenance** — Heartbeat-based periodic review, cleanup strategies, `heartbeat-state.json` tracking
5. **Advanced Patterns** — Entity tracking with stable headings, opinion evolution with timestamps, cross-session recall via `sessionMemory`
6. **Troubleshooting** — No results, keyword-only matches, `memory_get` file restrictions, MEMORY.md bloat, missing transcript search

### Navigation

Added to `docs.json` under Sessions and memory → Memory group, right after `concepts/memory`.

### Source references

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/backend-config.ts` — default settings (maxResults: 6, maxSnippetChars: 700)
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/read-file.ts` — `memory_get` file boundary enforcement
- `src/agents/memory-search.ts` — search config resolution and sources
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md` — existing builtin engine docs

Closes #43032

target.title: [codex] prefer terminal reply fields in CLI JSONL parser
target.body:
﻿﻿## Summary

- Problem: the CLI JSONL parser only special-cases Claude `type:"result"` events and otherwise falls back to generic text collection, so OpenAI/Codex-style fallback runs can lose terminal reply semantics.
- Why it matters: in channel-visible fallback paths, commentary/intermediate text can be surfaced instead of the actual final answer even when the JSONL stream already contains `phase:"final_answer"` and `task_complete.last_agent_message`.
- What changed: `parseCliJsonl()` now prefers `task_complete.last_agent_message`, then assistant messages tagged `phase:"final_answer"`, and skips `commentary`-phase generic item text.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Claude CLI handling is unchanged, no dispatch/channel code changed, and no provider failover logic changed.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #59918
- Related #25592
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: `parseCliJsonl()` was written around Claude `type:"result"` lines plus a generic `parsed.item.text` fallback, but it did not understand newer OpenAI/Codex-style JSONL terminal fields.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no parser preference for `task_complete.last_agent_message` or `phase:"final_answer"`, and no guard against treating `commentary` item text as the outbound reply.
- Prior context (`git blame`, prior PR, issue, or refactor if known): the current behavior is discussed in #59918 as a narrower parser-path issue adjacent to the broader channel-leak family in #25592.
- Why this regressed now: unknown as a specific regression point; this appears more like a compatibility gap exposed by fallback runs that emit richer JSONL event shapes.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: this fix does not depend on channel dispatching, failover selection, or Claude stream-json parsing.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/cli-output.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: when JSONL contains commentary, `final_answer`, and `task_complete`, the parser returns the terminal answer; when only `final_answer` is present, it wins over commentary text.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the bug lives entirely inside the JSONL parsing function and can be reproduced with synthetic line fixtures without needing a live provider or channel.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): existing Claude result tests in `src/agents/cli-output.test.ts` cover the Claude-specific path and remain unchanged.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- OpenAI/Codex-style CLI fallback runs now prefer terminal reply fields instead of surfacing commentary when both are present in JSONL.
- Commentary-only generic item text is no longer treated as the final reply in this parser path.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
CLI JSONL -> generic text collection -> commentary can win -> user sees wrong reply

After:
CLI JSONL -> task_complete / final_answer preferred -> terminal answer wins -> user sees final reply
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux (local contributor checkout)
- Runtime/container: Node.js + pnpm
- Model/provider: parser coverage for OpenAI/Codex-style CLI JSONL output; Claude path rechecked via existing tests
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A for unit verification
- Relevant config (redacted): CLI backend `output: "jsonl"`

### Steps

1. Feed `parseCliJsonl()` a JSONL stream containing commentary events plus a terminal `task_complete.last_agent_message`.
2. Feed `parseCliJsonl()` a JSONL stream containing commentary plus assistant `phase:"final_answer"` content.
3. Run the targeted parser tests.

### Expected

- Terminal answer fields win over commentary.
- Claude JSONL result handling still passes unchanged.

### Actual

- Verified with targeted tests after the patch.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/cli-output.test.ts src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts`
- Edge cases checked: existing Claude stream-json tests still pass; `task_complete` outranks `final_answer`; `final_answer` outranks commentary; commentary `item.text` is ignored.
- What you did **not** verify: I did not run a live WhatsApp/Telegram fallback end-to-end against a real CLI provider from this branch.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: OpenAI/Codex-style CLI JSONL output is now parsed so terminal reply records win over commentary or intermediate message text in both the full-buffer parser and streaming parser.

Real environment tested: Windows/PowerShell checkout at PR head `8b90301ef3`; installed OpenAI Codex CLI `codex-cli 0.130.0-alpha.5`; Node `v24.13.1`; OpenClaw parser entry points imported directly from `src/agents/cli-output.ts`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
codex exec --json --ephemeral --ignore-rules --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check "Reply exactly: FINAL_PROOF_IGNORE_RULES_OK" 1> .artifacts/real-proof-59920/codex-ignore-rules.jsonl 2> .artifacts/real-proof-59920/codex-ignore-rules.stderr.txt

node --import tsx --input-type=module
imports parseCliJsonl() and createCliJsonlStreamingParser() from ./src/agents/cli-output.ts
feeds the saved Codex CLI JSONL transcript through both parser paths

node --import tsx --input-type=module
imports the same parser entry points and replays redacted Codex/OpenAI terminal-field JSONL containing commentary, final_answer, and task_complete records
```

Evidence after fix:

```text
$ codex exec --json --ephemeral --ignore-rules --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check "Reply exactly: FINAL_PROOF_IGNORE_RULES_OK"
{"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"019e228b-0ab8-7ea1-9675-ea6149bafe95"}
{"type":"turn.started"}
{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_0","type":"agent_message","text":"FINAL_PROOF_IGNORE_RULES_OK"}}
{"type":"turn.completed","usage":{"input_tokens":22858,"cached_input_tokens":2432,"output_tokens":129,"reasoning_output_tokens":116}}

real_codex_full_buffer_output=
{"text":"FINAL_PROOF_IGNORE_RULES_OK","sessionId":"019e228b-0ab8-7ea1-9675-ea6149bafe95","usage":{"input":22858,"output":129,"cacheRead":2432}}
real_codex_streaming_output=
{"text":"FINAL_PROOF_IGNORE_RULES_OK","sessionId":"019e228b-0ab8-7ea1-9675-ea6149bafe95","usage":{"input":22858,"output":129,"cacheRead":2432}}
```

```text
terminal_field_jsonl=
{"type":"response_start","thread_id":"thread-real-proof-redacted"}
{"item":{"type":"message","phase":"commentary","text":"COMMENTARY_SHOULD_NOT_WIN"}}
{"type":"response_item","payload":{"type":"message","role":"assistant","phase":"final_answer","content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"FINAL_ANSWER_SHOULD_BE_OVERRIDDEN"}]}}
{"type":"event_msg","payload":{"type":"task_complete","last_agent_message":"TASK_COMPLETE_WINS"}}

{"text":"TASK_COMPLETE_WINS","sessionId":"thread-real-proof-redacted"}

{"text":"TASK_COMPLETE_WINS","sessionId":"thread-real-proof-redacted"}
```

Observed result after fix: The installed Codex CLI produced JSONL on this machine and both OpenClaw parser paths extracted the final agent message from that transcript. For the bot-cited terminal-field shape, both parser paths returned `TASK_COMPLETE_WINS`; `COMMENTARY_SHOULD_NOT_WIN` and the lower-priority `FINAL_ANSWER_SHOULD_BE_OVERRIDDEN` were not surfaced.

What was not tested: A live WhatsApp/Telegram delivery route was not exercised for this parser-only PR.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: a non-Claude JSONL backend could intentionally rely on commentary-phase `item.text` as the only final output.
  - Mitigation: the parser now only skips explicit `commentary` phase text and prefers explicit terminal fields; generic non-commentary `item.text` fallback remains intact.

target.title: feat(doctor): add Node.js runtime info health contribution
target.body:
## Summary
Add a new Doctor health contribution that displays Node.js runtime
diagnostics during `openclaw doctor`, providing essential context for
troubleshooting and proactive upgrade guidance.
## What it does
**Runtime summary note** (always shown):
Node 24.14.0 · ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node · via nvm
**Version manager detection** — identifies nvm, fnm, volta, asdf, n,
nodenv, nodebrew, and nvs from the executable path.
**Proactive warnings** (when applicable):
- Node version below minimum (>=22.19.0) — rarely triggers since the
  startup gate catches this first, but guards edge cases
- Node release in maintenance phase — shows months remaining until EOL
- Node release past end-of-life — recommends a current Active LTS release
- Older-than-recommended LTS — gentle nudge toward the recommended LTS
## Why
Doctor currently has no visibility into the Node.js runtime environment.
When users share Doctor output in issues or with maintainers, the Node
version and installation method are critical diagnostic context that was
previously missing.
This reuses existing infrastructure:
- `runtime-guard.ts` — `detectRuntime()`, `parseSemver()`, `runtimeSatisfies()`
- `runtime-paths.ts` — `isVersionManagedNodePath()`
No new dependencies. No runtime behavior changes outside of Doctor.
## Changes
New files:
- `src/commands/doctor-node-runtime.ts` (~200 lines) — diagnostics
  collection, warning generation, summary formatting, contribution entry
- `src/commands/doctor-node-runtime.test.ts` — 27 unit tests
Modified:
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` — +1 import, +1 wrapper
  function, +1 contribution registration (after `bundled-plugin-runtime-deps`,
  before `state-integrity`)
## Test plan
- `pnpm check` — 0 errors ✅
- `vitest` — 27/27 tests ✅
- `pnpm build` — clean ✅
Test coverage:
- `detectVersionManagerName`: 11 tests (null, system, nvm, fnm, volta,
  asdf, n, nodenv, nodebrew, nvs, Windows backslash)
- `collectNodeRuntimeDiagnostics`: 3 tests (nvm path, unknown runtime,
  system install)
- `buildNodeRuntimeWarnings`: 8 tests (recommended version, below
  minimum, past EOL, maintenance phase, pre-maintenance nudge, current
  recommended, null major, future major)
- `buildNodeRuntimeSummary`: 5 tests (system install, named manager,
  unknown manager, null version, separator format)
---
## Real behavior proof
_Refreshed for current head `f90eee0a` (after the Windows case-insensitive OS-home redaction commit)._

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The Doctor Node runtime note renders the executable path via a two-pass redaction (`shortenHomePath` for the OpenClaw home, then an OS-home pass). The OS-home pass compared the Windows home prefix with exact casing, so a valid Windows path whose drive/username casing differed from `os.homedir()` (e.g. `os.homedir()` = `C:\Users\Alice`, `execPath` = `c:\users\alice\...`) fell through unredacted and leaked the OS username. POSIX comparison stays case-sensitive; the Windows backslash-boundary prefix is now compared case-insensitively, slicing by the original length to preserve real casing.

- **Real environment tested:** Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, WSL2), Node.js 24.14.0, current PR head `f90eee0a`. Invoked the real `collectNodeRuntimeDiagnostics()` + `buildNodeRuntimeSummary()` — the same render `noteNodeRuntime()` emits in the Doctor health flow — plus injected lifecycle scenarios via the exported helpers.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ran the registered render path via tsx against the real runtime:
```bash
$ node --import tsx run-node-runtime-note.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix (current head):** Block 1 is the real render on this machine. Block 2 is the POSIX OS-home redaction scenario (OPENCLAW_HOME elsewhere). Block 3 is the new Windows case-insensitive redaction this commit fixes. Remaining blocks are injected lifecycle scenarios against the current date.
```
=== 1. Real current-head render (Node v24.14.0) ===
Node 24.14.0 · /usr/bin/node · system install

=== 2. POSIX OS-home redaction (OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw, Node under the user's OS home) ===
os home (HOME)     : /home/<user>
input  execPath    : /home/<user>/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node
output rendered    : Node 24.14.0 · ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node · via nvm
leaks OS username? : NO (redacted)

=== 3. Windows case-insensitive redaction (the new fix) ===
os.homedir()       : C:\Users\Alice   (canonical casing)
input  execPath    : c:\users\alice\AppData\Roaming\nvm\v24.14.0\node.exe   (lower-cased)
output rendered    : Node 24.14.0 · ~\AppData\Roaming\nvm\v24.14.0\node.exe · via nvm
leaks OS username? : NO (redacted)

=== Injected Node 22 LTS (22.19.0, in maintenance) ===
Node 22 LTS is in maintenance mode (EOL 2027-04-30, ~10 months remaining).
Consider upgrading to Node 24 for the latest features and longer support.

=== Injected Node 20 (20.18.0, below the >=22.19.0 minimum) ===
Node 20.18.0 does not meet the minimum requirement (>=22.19.0).
Upgrade Node: https://nodejs.org/en/download
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The real Node 24.14.0 runtime renders a clean note (supported, system install). Both the POSIX OS-home scenario (block 2) and the Windows case-mismatch scenario (block 3) now redact the home to `~`, so no OS username appears — including when `execPath` casing differs from `os.homedir()`. Before this commit, the exact-case Windows prefix check left such paths unredacted. Injected Node 22 LTS / 20 produce the expected maintenance / below-minimum advisories. POSIX, Windows OPENCLAW_HOME-override, and the new Windows case-mismatch regression tests cover the redaction paths; 51 unit tests pass, types and lint clean.

- **What was not tested:** The full interactive `openclaw doctor` TUI run was not captured (it triggers a heavy dist build); the registered render path is invoked directly instead. Redaction relies on `os.homedir()`; in the rare case where `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` is unset and differs from the path's owner (e.g. some sudo/container setups), redaction may not apply — out of scope for this detect-only diagnostic.
